finishes.note: Inner faces of the four walls from the floor to the vaults' wall arches, and the 18 responds' pilasters: Burgundy pressed brick 220 x 105 x 55 in lime mortar, English bond (Story: the Reserve's piers, arches and vaults).
The 14 piers' chamfered shafts 0.70 square, 40 mm chamfers in cut brick, 0.54-3.64.
The 24 groin vaults' webs: half-brick shells 0.105 normal to the intrados, stretcher bond, courses parallel to each barrel's axis, cut brick at the groins.
The 21 cross bands and 16 arcade bands (with their lunette faces): the web shell deepened 0.06, square arrises.
The west door's jambs and semicircular soffit through the 0.60 wall: two rowlock rings, headers on the soffit.
Never seen: the haunch fill to the box's top, the box's outer faces and top (waterproofed back), and the flat brick bed under the floor flags (z -0.35 to -0.06). Solid, sealed.
Pier bases (square-splayed profile) and the respond bases; vein-cut, voids filled, kicked soft at the arrises.
Pier imposts (square-splayed profile) and the respond impost blocks; the springing of every arch at 4.00; voids open.
The doorway detail's surround on the hall face of the west door: the museum's slim architrave P6 (architrave.two-fascia.160), honed in every era (Story section 4).

The nave's flags (|y| <= 4.65) 0.750 x 0.750 x 0.060, 3 mm lime joints on the 0.75 grid: Belgian bluestone (Petit Granit, Soignies), honed; the Paris cellar floor (Story: replaces the dark polished concrete).
The same flags in the two aisles and between the piers (|y| > 4.65); split from reserve.floor only so the aisles carry their own light target.
The 36 flush floor tracks: bronze channels lining the guide slots, 20 mm clear x 45 deep, 5 mm lips flush with the flags; brushed, walked bright (Story: rack tracks, flush).
The 36 overhead tracks (channel, nave-end stop, wall plate and bolts, clamps) and their hanger rods, collars and canopies: statuary-brown patina, waxed.
Each rack's frame: two end posts 0.090 x 0.160 and the top and kick rails, drawn and rolled CuZn30 hollow sections, clear-lacquered (Story: rack frames).

The rack's face: crimped woven wire mesh of CuZn30 wire dia 3.0 mm at 25 mm pitch (22 mm square aperture), one sheet in the rack's centre plane, clamped in the frame; clear-lacquered (Story: woven wire mesh).
The carriage on each rack: two trolley saddles, stems and nuts (and their wheels in the track), two guide shoes and two guide fins; relieved bright where they rub (Story: rack carriages, patinated).
The pull on each rack's nave-end post: bar dia 22 on two stand-offs; patina worn to bright bronze by hands.
The picture-light troughs 64 x 44 and their two arms and rail plates on the eight lit faces.
The 24 pendants' globes: Lamberts cased opal, mouth-blown, dia 0.44 (nave) and 0.34 (aisles), neck and rolled lip (Palette: Reserve globes).
Galleries (spun 1.5 mm), socket cups, canopies, the nave chains and loops, the aisle rods dia 15 with swivel balls and locknuts, thumb screws (Palette: globe rods, patinated).
The 56 impost uplights' cans dia 44 x 75, bezels and knuckle stems, and the easel spot's canopy, stem and head.
The viewing easel's runners, cross foot, uprights, rails, ledge and lip: quartersawn sessile oak (Story: the Reserve's easel, oiled and hard-waxed).
The easel's two caps and two ledge brackets (as built brass; brass stays only for the racks' drawn and woven parts, Story 2.3).
The four plan-chest islands: carcasses, tops and the 80 drawer fronts, fumed with ammonia and waxed (Story: replaces the as-built walnut).
The drawer pulls, bars 140 x 18, 22 proud (as built brass).
The chests' recessed plinths, 50 mm set back, 0.09 high; toe-scuffed.
The two felt mats under the Degas pastels on the south islands, 5 mm, undyed grey-green wool felt (Palette: the Reserve's mats).
Every oil's frame (Hang frame): carved oak, gesso, water-gilt on red bole, 0.090 face; the Salon's frame, bole on the worn ridges; Art builds it.
The pastels' window mats (80 mm border; Tub 0.99 x 0.76, Star 0.58 x 0.74), cotton museum board, bevel-cut; Art's mount (the Hang frame of the two pastels).
The glazing over each pastel's mat on a 6 mm spacer (a pastel is never kept bare): Optiwhite laminated with a UV-filtering interlayer.
Only on the Reserve's own stand (nympheas absent): a closed pair of cast bronze leaves in the class opening on the port face. Tonight the blind is the oval's (nympheas.stair.blind-doors).
